overall: The AG found no evidence the Everett School Finance Review Commission violated the Open Meeting Law after a member of the public was removed and members stayed to talk; it declined the adjournment-motion allegation and issued a non-binding caution.

allegations.summary: A member of the public was told to leave a commission meeting while a quorum of members remained in the room.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we recommend that public bodies, to avoid the appearance of impropriety, not eject members of the public from meeting rooms while a quorum of the public body remains, unless they will be entering into a proper executive session.

allegations.summary: After the public was removed, several commission members stayed and talked in small groups, allegedly about commission business outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we credit the Commission’s assertion that the members did not talk about Commission business after the meeting had been adjourned and therefore find that the Commission did not deliberate outside of the public meeting.

allegations.summary: The meeting was allegedly not properly adjourned because no motion was made to formally conclude it.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.
